entries.reads: a recorder of both pasted codes and the server's rows, with a later CRQC, reads the epoch a founding add admitted the joiner at
the same recorder reads the epoch a live add (a rotated pq_secret) admitted the joiner at
the same recorder reads the epoch an admin's add admitted the joiner at, in a group of four: the adder hands on secrets it was itself handed

a recorder of a second device's pasted codes, handed the exporter of the classical join, finds the join epoch's secret and the group's handle key in the invitation; the device is added by a plain member that holds the identity, and no canary is read
the recorder holds the invitation and not the join code, so the CRQC has no init key to invert and reads nothing
both codes, with random octets where the pq_secret would be: the read goes through that one value and nothing else
both codes plus the true pq_secret and group_handle_key handed to the recorder: the pipeline reads exactly the join epoch
a classical observer of one pasted invitation plus the server's rows recovers group_handle_key, which maps every sender_handle to a leaf for the group's life
with no key at all, the order sender handles first appear in the server's rows links the founder and this paste's joiner to their handles; sealing the secrets does not change it
an attacker on the paste channel rewrites the invitation so that it carries secrets the attacker chose, and the joiner installs them
an invitation refused for naming another group costs the joiner its one-use join code, so the honest invitation that follows cannot be joined
an invitation refused after the engine has joined costs the joiner its join code and leaves state behind
a swapper substitutes its own join code; the founder adds the swapper believing it is the victim, and the swapper reads what the founder sends
a copy of the joiner's state directory taken after the join reads the join epoch: keys at rest are plaintext
the recorder also holds the joiner's X-Wing seed, copied before the join: it opens the recorded seal and reads the join epoch. The seal is to a static key

the same, for a live add: the seed and the recording read the epoch the rotated secret was sealed for. It is the live road's control that the recorder still reads when the seal is the only thing in its way
a valid invitation into an attacker's group founded under a group id the victim holds replaces the victim's group
the same invitation, bent so that it is refused after the engine has joined, still replaces the held group's epoch state
an invitation that names a fresh group id and carries a welcome for the held group replaces the held group's epoch state
the victim has restarted and not restored: the group is on its disk and not in its memory, and the invitation replaces it
the victim joined above epoch one, so the hostile welcome stands at an epoch it holds no state for: only the held-group gate itself is in the way
both at once: on disk and not in memory, at an epoch the victim holds no state for; only the gate's reading of the records on the disk is in the way

a second founder's invitation, standing above the epoch of the removal, into a group of its own under the id of a group this device was removed from: the record is replaced and the device no longer reads as removed

a group whose record is on the disk and whose epoch states are gone does not restore; it is left with ForgetGroup, the founder removes the stranded leaf and adds a fresh join code, and the device joins again

one group record on the device's disk does not read: every other group restores and the damage is reported, another group still joins, a fresh id still founds, a founding under the damaged group's id and an invitation into it are refused while the record stands, and the group is left with ForgetGroup and joined again over the same invitation
